The University of Virginia seeks applications for an Academic Support Program Coordinator to work as part of the STEM Support Services team. Our mission is to support students’ learning in gateway courses so that they are well-positioned to pursue STEM-related majors and post-graduation goals. More broadly, we aim to contribute to a collaborative, positive learning environment for students pursuing these goals. Our programs include Peer Led Learning (P2L), which is a supplemental-instruction style, collaborative group program, as well as Peer Academic Coaching (one-on-one, by-appointment support) and the Math Collaborative Learning Center (drop-in support for math courses), and our scope includes lower-division courses across biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics.

The STEM Support Services team operates out of the Georges Student Center in Clemons Library. The coordinator will occasionally provide support in the Center's spaces or assist with special events. Position Summary

Position: Community Health Worker

Location: Field 75% or more of the time

Schedule: Mon-Fri 08:0-05:00 PM EST

The Community Health Worker (CHW) will support the implementation of the CHW Pilot designed to address health disparities, improve outcomes, and reduce avoidable utilization among Medicaid members with Type 2 diabetes. This role is critical in addressing identified needs, including high diabetes prevalence and significant social determinants of health (SDoH) risk within targeted counties. The CHW will engage directly with members to improve self-management, enhance access to care and community resources, and support overall health outcomes through culturally appropriate, community-based interventions.

The CHW will serve as a liaison between members, the care management team, providers, and community resources, with a focus on improving member experience, increasing primary care engagement, and reducing emergency department and inpatient utilization.

Position Responsibilities

Conduct telephonic, virtual, and face-to-face outreach and engagement with assigned members.
Maintain an active caseload (approximately up to 30 members), with engagement duration based on member needs.
Complete required screenings and assessments, including initial engagement and health equity screeners within required timeframes.
Develop and implement individualized action plans in collaboration with members and interdisciplinary care teams.
Provide education and support related to Type 2 diabetes management, including medication adherence, nutrition, physical activity, and lifestyle behaviors.
Identify and address gaps in care, supporting members in completing recommended preventive and follow-up services.
Connect members to community-based resources addressing SDoH needs (e.g., food, housing, transportation) and ensure closed-loop referral follow-up.
Assist members in navigating healthcare services, including scheduling and attending primary and specialty care appointments.
Participate in interdisciplinary team meetings and case rounds to support care coordination.
Document all member interactions, outreach attempts, and interventions in designated systems in accordance with program requirements.
Support member engagement in pilot initiatives and services, including education programs, community events, and resource utilization.
Promote positive member relationships and culturally competent care aligned with community needs.

Required Qualifications

Experience working in community health, social services, care management, or related field.
Experience engaging with underserved or high-risk populations.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and engagement skills.
Ability to build trust and maintain relationships with diverse populations.
Knowledge of community resources and SDoH-related services.
Ability to manage a caseload and document activities accurately.
Must live in Camden County or nearby

License / Credential Requirements

Community Health Worker (CHW) Certification from the NJ Department of Health (or must obtain within 12 months of employment date).

Preferred Qualifications

Lived experience or prior work supporting individuals with Type 2 diabetes or chronic conditions.
Experience working within Medicaid or managed care environments.
Bilingual or multilingual skills aligned with community served.
Familiarity with care management systems and electronic health records.
Knowledge of motivational interviewing, cultural competency, and trauma-informed care practices.

Education Required

High school diploma or equivalent required
Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Social Work, or related field preferred.

Founded in 2001, Mixteco/Indígena Community Organizing Project (MICOP) supports, organizes and empowers the indigenous migrant communities of California’s Central Coast through improved access to health and community resources, community organizing, language interpretation, education, direct assistance, cultural promotion, and our indigenous-led Radio Indígena community radio station. Summary

MICOP's OFY-RR Funds Project program takes a trauma-informed, youth-centered approach to supporting Indigenous and non-Indigenous Undocumented Unaccompanied Minors living in Ventura and County. The need to access resources, advocacy, and follow-up is extensive for both youth and their sponsors. The Coordinator is expected to provide leadership, guidance, and oversight to the OFY team while ensuring youth and their sponsors receive consistent, culturally responsive, and trauma-informed support.

Identify and partner with local community resource providers and maintain strong community partnership relationships.

Coordinate and assist in designing and implementing workshops, series, and reunions for youth and their sponsors.

Maintain confidentiality and ensure staff follow organizational, program, and data privacy requirements.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Experience in case management, youth services, community organizing, or working with immigrant and/or Indigenous communities is highly desired.

Passion for the mission of supporting, empowering, and organizing the Indigenous migrant community on California’s Central Coast.

Proven ability to prioritize workload, collaborate, and work effectively as part of a team.

Self-motivated with the ability to execute projects independently.

Demonstrated ability to use strength-based, youth-centered, and trauma-informed approaches to service delivery.

Ability to plan, organize, and execute program goals.

High proficiency in English and Spanish, both written and spoken.

Excellent interpersonal, communication, and verbal skills.

Are you looking for a career you can feel good about? We hire only those that strive to do their best. By joining our family, you'll receive the honor and recognition that comes with working for the industry's global leader in evidenced based rehabilitation.

Who We Are

GEO provides complementary, turnkey solutions for numerous government partners worldwide across a spectrum of diversified correctional and community reentry services. From the development of state-of-the-art facilities and the provision of management services and evidence-based rehabilitation to the post-release reintegration and supervision of individuals in the community, GEO offers fully diversified, cost-effective services that deliver enhanced quality and improved outcomes.

Why Work For GEO

We believe that work is more than a place you go to every day. It is about being inspired and motivated to achieve extraordinary things.
Employee benefits play an important role in making The GEO Group a great place to work. At GEO, we believe in the three pillars of employee wellbeing: physical, emotional, and financial. With comprehensive benefits and competitive wages, we trust that you will find all the resources you need here to be successful.

Responsibilities

Summary

This position is responsible for the facility programs and the counseling areas, supervision of all counseling staff including staff scheduling, training coordination, annual performance and file compliance. This position has the necessary knowledge and familiarity with ACA, DOC, and DDAP regulations to assure facility compliance with the regulatory standards. Finally, this position responsible to ensure smooth operation and coordination of program services including Inpatient D & A, Work Release and Outpatient Programming.

Primary Duties And Responsibilities

Oversees facility programs and counseling areas.
Provides direct supervision including staffing, schedules, re-entrant affairs and file compliance. Ensures all counseling staff is aware of their areas of responsibility. Evaluates Counselors’ performance of their duties including observation of re-entrant sessions and random file reviews.
Ensures that Counselors and programming complies with requirements of all referral sources and jurisdictions.
Organizes, implements and supervises the Correctional Recovery program as defined by the Program Manual.
Work closely with referral sources to ensure smooth operation and coordination of all program services.
Provides staff training and implementation of program design.
Provides and documents individual/group staff supervision.
Provides direct services including facilitation of classes/group sessions, individual counseling, treatment planning, assessment; document progress and reviews.
Leads the Classification Committee and ensures that intakes are conducted properly.
Completes training plans and records; ensures counseling staff participate in required training.
Develops and maintains knowledge of and familiarity with ACA, DOC, and DDAP Accreditation and ensures program compliance.
Writes social histories, clinical assessments, and develop treatment plans.
Monitors re-entrant progress toward goals and objectives as stated in the treatment plan and update the treatment as required.
Ensures re-entrant progress toward goals and objectives as stated in the Program Plan and update the Program Plan as required.
Prepares parole summaries, Extraordinary Occurrence reports, and Employee Report of Incidents.
Completes weekly and monthly reports as required for referring agencies.
Obtains funding for residents.
Assists clients with medical and mental health appointments, housing options, and other needs as they arise.
Develops a strong rapport with referring agencies and community agencies.
Submits required paperwork and documentation in a timely manner.
Supervises a caseload of up to eight inpatient re-entrants.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Master’s degree in behavioral sciences or appropriate discipline.
Two (2) years related clinical supervisory experience.
Demonstrated supervisory experience.
Licensure in the behavioral science or counseling field and certification in the behavioral science or counseling field.
Good visual and auditory abilities to interact with re-entrants.
